title: Private SSO session fingerprint entropy mismatch causing role mapping race and audit log corruption
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Several private customers reported intermittent RBAC failures and missing audit entries after a routine IdP certificate rollover. Root behavior: session fingerprints generated by the private-SSO bridge have non-deterministic entropy changes across short time windows. This leads to transient mismatches between the assertion->role mapping cache and the RBAC enforcer, causing users to briefly lose permissions. In parallel, the audit writer sometimes receives truncated assertion IDs which results in corrupted audit rows and gaps in the audit timeline. Affected components: private-ssoproxy (session fingerprinting), rbacauth (role mapper cache), audit-writer (bulk flush path).
root_cause: During the IdP certificate rollover a change in the underlying randomness source (explicit reseeding in the platform agent) combined with a previously unnoticed timing race in fingerprint generation caused identical assertions processed at near-simultaneous times to receive different fingerprints. The RBAC role mapping cache key used the fingerprint as the primary key; when two fingers for the same assertion diverged briefly, parallel request processing created competing cache entries. The audit-writer relies on stable assertion IDs for idempotent writes; when the fingerprint changed mid-processing the writer merged partial rows and triggered a compression path that resulted in truncated payloads. The root is a combination of (1) non-deterministic entropy reseed during cert rotation, (2) cache-key design coupling to volatile fingerprint, (3) audit writer flush path not handling identical-but-variant IDs atomically.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a private control plane with scheduled IdP cert rollover enabled. 2) Simulate burst logins from the same assertion (use load generator script attached in links). 3) Observe rapid fingerprint changes in private-ssoproxy logs (log key: ssoproxy.fingerprint.delta). 4) Trigger role mapping lookups and watch rbacauth logs for duplicate cache entries. 5) Inspect audit-writer outputs in S3/elastic (see example in links) and note truncated assertion IDs and missing sequence numbers.
mitigation: Immediate: 1) Temporarily set the private-ssoproxy config flag 'sso.stable_fingerprint=true' to force the legacy deterministic HMAC path; this prevents entropy reseed usage. 2) Apply an emergency watchdog in rbacauth to coalesce cache keys for a 500ms window (feature-flagged). 3) For customers with active escalations, enable a read-only audit-forwarding fallback to replicate missing entries to the compliance store. Operational: schedule a rolling restart of ssoproxy pods after enabling the flag to pick up the config change.
proposed_fix: Short term: Replace on-the-fly reseeding with a monotonic per-process salt stored in memory for the life of the process; update fingerprint algorithm to incorporate assertion stable-id + monotonic salt and timestamp bucket to avoid microsecond variance. Make rbacauth cache key tolerant to canonical assertion IDs and add a short de-duplication window. Harden audit-writer to verify payload integrity and requeue partial writes rather than compressing. Long term: introduce explicit assertion canonicalization API at the control plane boundary and add integration tests for IdP rotations.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge fix branch (PR linked). 2) Canary deploy to non-prod private cluster and run load generator for 30 minutes. 3) Canary to 3 low-risk customer private clusters with active support observers. 4) If stable for 24h, roll to remaining private clusters in waves of 10 with automated health checks. 5) Post-rollout monitor: RBAC error rate, audit-write error rate, and customer escalations channel for 48h. Feature flags: sso.stable_fingerprint, rbacauth.coalesce_window.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add end-to-end automated test covering IdP cert rotation under load. 2) Remove coupling between volatile fingerprint and cache key. 3) Create runbook for IdP rotations with preflight checks for randomness reseed. 4) Add alerting for audit-writer truncation and increase retention of raw audit writes for 7 days. 5) Hold cross-team review with Security and Platform to align on randomness and fingerprinting standards.
communication_plan: Customer comms: Draft sent to affected customers (link). For high-impact customers join weekly sync and share mitigation steps and ETA. Internal: update SRE incident channel, create support KB with rollback steps and support attachments. Legal/compliance: notify compliance lead and attach replicated audit copies for retention. Public: no public-facing advisory until patch verified.
